key_insight: MEOWN is a physics-informed machine-learning framework that rapidly predicts energetically favorable muon stopping sites in crystals by combining electrostatics, screening, polarization, symmetry, and zero-point motion.
engineering_relevance: It can dramatically reduce the cost and turnaround time of muon-site calculations, enabling faster interpretation of muon spectroscopy in quantum and magnetic materials.
method: Uses a Polarizable Unperturbed Electrostatic Potential (P-UEP) model as the physics prior.
Guides site optimization with machine learning and symmetry-aware relaxation.
Incorporates electrostatic interactions, electronic screening, polarization, and zero-point motion for physically consistent predictions.
evidence_signal: The framework was benchmarked on MnSi, CoF2, CaF2, LiF, and NaF, and its predicted stopping sites and dipolar fields closely matched prior DFT+mu results while producing estimates in minutes.
watch_item: Performance is validated on a limited set of benchmark crystalline materials, so broader transferability may still depend on chemical diversity and careful implementation.
paper_title: Development of a Physics-Informed Neural Framework, MEOWN, for Rapid Prediction of Muon Stopping Sites in Crystalline Materials, for understanding Quantum Magnet employing Muon Spectroscopy
